subject: Weekly Fleet Planning: Dedicated Capacity Sizing & Pipeline Tie-in
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-01T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fleet planning sync — tying pipeline to GPU reservations

Team —

Following up from last quarter's post-mortem, we need to formalize a weekly cadence that ties sales pipeline commits to Dedicated capacity sizing. The ask for this week: can infra + finance give a reconciled view of the GPU inventory needed for signed & likely deals over next 90 days, and flag any gaps that would require procurement or temporary burst capacity?

Context / goals:
- Sales: convert committed deals without latency regressions. We should prefer reservation over burst where feasible to lock cost.
- Infra: plan for both steady-reserve and short-term burst (e.g., on-demand H100 pools) and identify any long lead times (hardware procurement or regional capacity limits).
- Finance: surface the P&L impact for committing GPUs vs using burst (include amortized cost & opportunity cost for credits).

Attached: Q1_pipeline_gpu_requirements.csv (first cut; rows = deals with forecasted start date, qps target, estimated GPU-hours/day) and a draft playbook for reserved vs burst handling.

Please reply with:
1) Dev — a conservative + optimistic GPU count and latency risk notes (by deal).
2) Grace — cost delta table for reserved vs burst for the same windows and recommended approval threshold.
3) Rishi / Hannah — confirm which deals are "committed" vs "best-effort" for next 60 days; call out any anchor customers that need guaranteed capacity.

I propose we meet Friday 10:00 PT for a 30-min run-through. If any of you need earlier, state now.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Q1_pipeline_gpu_requirements.csv (csv, 1 worksheet)
- dedicated_capacity_playbook_v2.pdf (pdf, draft)

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-01T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet planning sync — tying pipeline to GPU reservations

Thanks Marissa — I pulled the attached CSV and did a rapid sizing pass. High-level notes below (conservative vs optimistic assumptions):

Conservative (safety factor 1.4):
- Acme AI (DEAL-4857) — 40x A100 80GB sustained (or 32x H100 equiv) to meet 99th p95 latency targets for their gen endpoint at expected traffic (starting 2026-04-15).
- NimbusPay pilot — 8x A100 80GB for dedicated sandbox + burst allowance for tokenization flows (start 2026-03-20).
- Other small pilots (aggregate) — reserve 12x A100 pooled with autoscaling to handle spikes.
- Total conservative reserved footprint needed by 2026-04-15: 60x A100 (or capacity-equivalent mix).

Optimistic (safety factor 1.1):
- Total optimistic reserved footprint: 44x A100.

Operational constraints & notes:
- Lead time: procuring new H100s for on-prem ordering has a 6–10 week lead; cloud marketplace reserved capacity can be booked in 2–4 days but carries higher committed spend.
- Regional availability: us-west and us-east both have capacity but us-west bursts are more expensive ~12% premium.
- Cache/batching optimizations could reduce sustained GPU requirement by ~10–20% for retrieval-heavy workloads but we should not rely on this for firm commitments.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Hold a soft reservation for 40 A100-eq (cover optimistic -> conservative midpoint) through cloud-reserved SKU for 90 days while we finalize Acme commitment; this gives us immediate capacity and avoids procurement delay.
2) Run a week-long stress test on an infra replica cluster to validate p95 latency at scaled qps (I’ll need ops time next week).
3) I’ll attach a short .csv with node-level breakdown after lunch.

Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fleet planning sync — tying pipeline to GPU reservations

Marissa / team —

I ran a delta model for reserved vs burst for the 90-day window in the CSV (assumptions in the attached workbook):

- Reserved (cloud reserved SKU) for 60 A100-eq over 90 days: estimated incremental cost = $1.08M; amortized to deals: Acme covers ~65% under proposed SOW, NimbusPay covers ~8%, remainder internal credit pool.
- Burst/on-demand H100 for peak capacity (no reservation): estimated cost for same capacity/time = $1.44M.
- Break-even point for reservation vs burst at our utilization assumptions: 28 days of steady usage at >70% utilization.

Recommendation:
- Approve soft-reservation for 40 A100-eq immediately (capex/opex impact fits within Q1 reforecast) — Treasury can authorize up to $500k commit without exec signoff. Anything beyond that needs CFO approval.
- For Acme (DEAL-4857) — propose a credit framework: if they sign within 30 days, credit X% of reservation cost back as usage credits (proposal attached: draft_MAL_credits_proposal.pdf).

Risks:
- If Acme slips >45 days we will be holding reservation risk; consider clause in SOW for reservation pass-through or minimum committed months.

Happy to walk through the delta model on Friday.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
